jokes.explanation: Emotionally resonant character comedy. The taxonomy of male goodbye gestures ('awkward hug or lame cool-guy handshake') is funny in its specificity. The fact that neither option is good, and the implicit defeat of choosing the 'cool' option only to abandon it, is true to these characters. Bittersweet and funny.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey guys, I just want to say goodbye to this table properly. You've been a real friend to me.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Red team, you were solid. White team, you had your moments.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: And to all of you out there on the field... it's been an honor.

jokes.text: Airport security confirms phalange is fixed — 'Yes. The phalange's fixed. In fact, we've put a whole lot of extra phalanges onboard, just in case.'
jokes.setup: Passengers ask if the phalange problem has been fixed; staff need to manage the situation
jokes.punchline: Staff confirms the (fake) phalange is fixed and they've added 'extra phalanges just in case' — playing along with the fiction
jokes.explanation: Good final beat to the phalange saga. The staff's desperate commitment to the fiction — adding 'extra phalanges just in case' — is funny because it shows how deep the lie has gone. The bureaucratic doubling-down on a made-up part is a nice satirical touch.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait! You can't get on that plane!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Phoebe, what are you talking about?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I have a feeling something bad is going to happen on that plane.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: What? Phoebe, that's crazy.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: No! I'm telling you, I have a premonition. The левian core is gonna fail!

jokes.text: Flight attendant tells Rachel: 'The phalange is fixed. In fact, we've put a whole lot of extra phalanges onboard, just in case.'
jokes.setup: Passengers have been panicking about the missing phalange; the airline is trying to get them back on
jokes.punchline: The flight attendant doubles down by not only claiming the phalange is fixed but announcing they've added 'a whole lot of extra phalanges' — the airline is now committed to the fictional part
jokes.explanation: The airline's capitulation to the fiction — not just fixing the phalange but stockpiling extras — is a brilliant escalation. 'A whole lot of extra phalanges onboard, just in case' shows the institutional absurdism of an airline playing along with a made-up part. The structure is excellent: denial → repair → excess stock.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You know, I have to say, for a blind woman, I'm having a great time on this plane.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.line: Wait, you're blind?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.line: Oh my God!

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.line: *gets up and leaves*

jokes.text: 'What? Oh, my God. What are you guys doing here?' / 'Okay. You're on.' — Phoebe to Ross at the gate
jokes.setup: Ross and Phoebe have made it to the gate; Phoebe has been running interference with the boarding agent
jokes.punchline: 'Okay. You're on.' — Phoebe hands off to Ross like a stage manager handing off to a performer
jokes.explanation: Good Phoebe line. Her theatrical 'You're on' frames the romantic moment as a performance she's been setting up — perfectly in keeping with her character's flair for drama. Light but effective.

dialogue.speaker: Flight Attendant
dialogue.line: Sir, that's not correct. We're not going down.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.line: Oh my God, we're not going down? Then where are we going?

jokes.text: Ross and Rachel finally reunite. After a long tender moment: 'It's you and me, all right? This is it.' Rachel: 'This is it. Unless we're on a break.'
jokes.setup: Ross and Rachel have declared their love and committed to being together permanently
jokes.punchline: Rachel drops 'unless we're on a break' — the season-long, series-long running gag — in the most tender possible moment
jokes.explanation: The second-best joke in the episode and arguably the perfect final joke for Ross and Rachel's arc. Ten seasons of 'we were on a break' are condensed into this single throwaway line from Rachel — delivered in the middle of their most romantic moment. It works because it's simultaneously an acknowledgment of their history, a joke at Ross's expense, and a sign of Rachel's affection (she's teasing him, not fighting him). The structure is perfect: maximum emotion → maximum comedy → perfect character note. 'Don't make jokes now' is the ideal response.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Tools are a crutch. They distance you from the work.

jokes.text: Monica, watching the movers: 'Okay, please be careful with that. It was my grandmother's. Be careful.' Joey: 'If that falls off the truck, it wouldn't be the worst thing.'
jokes.setup: Monica is anxiously supervising the movers with her grandmother's piece of furniture
jokes.punchline: Joey's aside 'if that falls off the truck, it wouldn't be the worst thing' implies the furniture is ugly/unwanted
jokes.explanation: Joey's aside is a classic 'this family heirloom is terrible' joke. Functional and in character but not particularly novel.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh no, the baby birds fell out of the nest. I gotta put them back.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait a minute... how do I know these are even my kids?

jokes.text: In the empty apartment: 'Has it always been purple?'
jokes.setup: The gang stands in Monica's empty apartment for the last time
jokes.punchline: Chandler, apparently seeing the wall color for the first time now that furniture is removed, asks if it's always been purple
jokes.explanation: Perfect bittersweet comedy. The apartment has been a primary set for ten seasons; the purple walls are iconic. Chandler noticing for the first time — after a decade — is a genuine laugh. The simplicity of the question carries the weight of ten years.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, check it out! I'm gonna get a couple of ducks, maybe a goose. Oh! And a chicken!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, no.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: What? It'll be like a farm!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: A farm? Joey, you can barely take care of yourself.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm gonna call it 'Joey's Farm.' It's gonna be huge!

jokes.text: Monica: 'Because of rent control, it was a frigging steal.'
jokes.setup: Monica is giving a speech about the apartment being a happy place filled with love and laughter
jokes.punchline: She pivots from sentimental to practical — the most important thing about the apartment was that it was a 'frigging steal' via rent control
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's most satisfying laugh-through-tears moments. Monica's sentimental speech veers into the most Monica-possible observation — the financial value of rent control. The pivot from 'love and laughter' to 'frigging steal' is a perfect tonal subversion. Also a winking acknowledgment of the show's famous implausibility (how does Monica afford this apartment on a chef's salary?). Great character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm going to get a goose.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: A goose? Joey, where are you going to keep a goose?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I don't know, I'll figure it out.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh sure, because that's worked out so well for you in the past.

jokes.text: Ross's summer as a dancer: 'What about that summer during college that you lived with Grandma and you tried to make it as a dancer?' Ross: 'Do you realize we almost made it 10 years without that coming up?'
jokes.setup: Joey says he never lived in the apartment; Monica and Chandler recall people who did
jokes.punchline: Monica brings up Ross's failed attempt to 'make it as a dancer' — an embarrassing backstory presumably never mentioned in 10 seasons
jokes.explanation: Ross's indignant 'we almost made it 10 years without that coming up' is both funny and meta — it's a wink at the fact that this is indeed the series finale. The 'dancer' detail for Ross is unexpected and perfect. The 10-year timeframe also directly references the show's run.

dialogue.speaker: Flight Attendant
dialogue.line: Ladies and gentlemen, I know you're all concerned about that part we found in the cockpit, but I want to assure you that it's probably not important. In fact, I'm sure the plane is better off without it. So just sit back, relax, and try not to think about which part of the plane might fall off next.

jokes.text: 'Do you realize we almost made it 10 years without that coming up?'
jokes.setup: Monica has just revealed Joey's secret dancer past
jokes.punchline: Joey's response treats the near-decade of secrecy as an accomplishment that Monica has just spoiled
jokes.explanation: Perfect button for joke #93. The '10 years' framing is a great meta-finale joke — this is literally the last episode of a 10-year show. Joey's indignant precision ('we almost made it') is both funny and characteristically Joey. Very well-constructed self-referential beat.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I'm not messing around anymore. We're done with the games.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I agree. No more of this on-and-off thing.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Right. And just to be clear... we are NOT on a break.

jokes.text: Final scene: Everyone leaves Monica's apartment. Final line from one character: 'Should we get some coffee?' / 'Sure. Where?' [looking at Central Perk]
jokes.setup: The group is leaving the apartment together for the last time
jokes.punchline: 'Where?' — the question is absurd because they always go to Central Perk, which is right downstairs. The 'where' acknowledges that the habitual, never-questioned routine is now genuinely open
jokes.explanation: The perfect series finale button. 'Where?' has 23 minutes of meaning packed into one word — the coffee shop they've gone to for ten years is downstairs, but their world is changing. The question is simultaneously funny (it's obvious) and genuinely poignant (it's not). One of the most elegant series-ending jokes in sitcom history. The craft is in the economy: the entire theme of the finale (change, uncertainty, the end of an era) lives in that single word.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: We were on a break!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ross, we were together for three years. You don't just get to use that one line forever.

tmdb_overview:
